_about: The English frames of every menu screen and the level texts, as numbers: every quad EmitMenu, EmitHud and EmitNotifications produce (planning step 238, PORT-34) - the rectangle, the uv, the colour and the turn, the picture's file name as a hash and the clamp. A suite compares what the layer draws now with these within a tolerance (the rectangle, in fractions of the window, 0.001; the other fractions 0.00001), so that a last-bit difference of the C library's sin and cos does not fail it and a moved glyph does. The numbers were dumped from the wired layer in the very run that first checked the layer's frames against the bit-hash golden recorded BEFORE the languages were wired in (every frame equal, bit for bit), so the default language is proven to draw what it always drew. A golden is never re-recorded to make a change pass: if English changed on purpose, the step says so and records why. FORMAT 3 (review of steps 236 to 239, finding F3): a glyph quad's uv rectangle is the character's cell on the original font's page, so the glyph quads of a frame that draws Asantee's achievements words (the dashboard, the achievements popup, a card for an achievement - the frames marked hidden) would spell them out of this file with the original's .fnt files. Those frames therefore carry no glyph quad here: only their other quads, their number of glyphs, the rectangle the glyphs fill, and ONE fingerprint (the top-level one) of the glyph sequences of all the hidden frames together - cells of the font pages in draw order, with how many other quads were drawn before each, no place. Their glyphs in full are in menu_screens_text_golden.json beside out/data/achievements.json (gitignored, never committed), written by this same command and compared when it is there. What is still stored and true: no pixel; no word of Asantee's achievements; but the glyph quads of every other frame, which spell only Enhanced's own words (game/data/lang), numbers and percents, and so are still the original fonts' atlas geometry for those characters.
